arxiv-2202-11857.description: Abstract Given a matching between n n red points and n n blue points by line segments in the plane, we consider the problem of obtaining a crossing-free matching through flip operations that replace two crossing segments by two non-crossing ones.

arxiv-2405-14705.title: Learning Multi-dimensional Human Preference for Text-to-Image Generation
arxiv-2405-14705.creator: Sixian Zhang, Bohan Wang, Junqiang Wu, Yan Li, Tingting Gao, Di Zhang, Zhongyuan Wang
arxiv-2405-14705.description: Abstract Current metrics for text-to-image models typically rely on statistical metrics which inadequately represent the real preference of humans. Although recent work attempts to learn these preferences via human annotated images, they reduce the rich tapestry of human preference to a single overall score. However, the preference results vary when humans evaluate images with different aspects.

arxiv-2408-15325.title: Deep thermalization under charge-conserving quantum dynamics
arxiv-2408-15325.creator: Rui-An Chang, Harshank Shrotriya, Wen Wei Ho, Matteo Ippoliti
arxiv-2408-15325.description: Abstract “Deep thermalization” describes the emergence of universal wavefunction distributions in quantum many-body dynamics, appearing on a local subsystem upon measurement of its environment. In this work, we study in detail the effect of continuous internal symmetries and associated conservation laws on deep thermalization.

arxiv-2512-11853.title: Evolving Deep Learning Optimizers
arxiv-2512-11853.creator: Mitchell Marfinetz
arxiv-2512-11853.description: Abstract We present a genetic algorithm framework for automatically discovering deep learning optimization algorithms. Our approach encodes optimizers as genomes that specify combinations of primitive update terms (gradient, momentum, RMS normalization, Adam-style adaptive terms, and sign-based updates) along with hyperparameters and scheduling options.

pmc-11363148.title: Advances in Extracellular-Vesicles-Based Diagnostic and Therapeutic Approaches for Ocular Diseases
pmc-11363148.creator: Yun Su, Moxin Chen, Wei Xu, Ping Gu, Xianqun Fan
pmc-11363148.description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are nanoscale membrane vesicles of various sizes that can be secreted by most cells. EVs contain a diverse array of cargo, including RNAs, lipids, proteins, and other molecules with functions of intercellular communication, immune modulation, and regulation of physiological and pathological processes.

pmc-11445000.title: Extracellular vesicles affecting embryo development in vitro: a potential culture medium supplement
pmc-11445000.creator: Yamei Xue, Haixia Zheng, Yuping Xiong, Kun Li
pmc-11445000.description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are nanometer-sized lipid bilayer vesicles released by cells, playing a crucial role in mediating cellular communication. This review evaluates the effect of EVs on early embryonic development in vitro by systematically searching the literature across three databases, Embase, PubMed, and Scopus, from inception (Embase, 1947; PubMed, 1996; and Scopus, 2004) to 30 June 2024.

pmc-11670271.title: Automated Microfluidics‐Assisted Hydrogel‐Based Wet‐Spinning for the Biofabrication of Biomimetic Engineered Myotendinous Junction
pmc-11670271.creator: Marina Volpi, Alessia Paradiso, Ewa Walejewska, Cesare Gargioli, Marco Costantini, Wojciech Swieszkowski
pmc-11670271.description: The muscle‐tendon junction (MTJ) plays a pivotal role in efficiently converting the muscular contraction into a controlled skeletal movement through the tendon. Given its complex biomechanical intricacy, the biofabrication of such tissue interface represents a significant challenge in the field of musculoskeletal tissue engineering.

pmc-12591625.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ary concern is the exclusion of standard and generally accepted techniques of screening, joint safety planning, patient education, lethal means counseling, follow-up contacts, and the involvement of friends and family. They rightly point out that the Rosen chapter1 and the guidelines from which it is derived2 should not be taken to define the clinical “standard of care,” which is why we avoided this terminology in our review.

pmc-13325957.title: Maternal cafeteria diet and methyl donor supplementation modulate gut microbiota and anxiety-like behavior in male offspring
pmc-13325957.creator: Ximena Rodríguez Gómez, Heriberto Castro, Alberto Camacho-Morales
pmc-13325957.description: Maternal cafeteria diet and methyl donor supplementation modulate gut microbiota and behavioral outcomes in male offspring.BackgroundMaternal hypercaloric diets rich in saturated fats and refined sugars are associated with metabolic alterations, gut microbiota dysbiosis, and behavioral disturbances in offspring. Methyl donor supplementation has been proposed as a potential strategy to modulate these effects.

pmc-13605439.title: Quantifying the Resolution Ceiling of Prototype-Based Few-Shot Segmentation on Sub-Centimetre Pulmonary Nodules: A Training-Free Geometric Analysis
pmc-13605439.creator: Joon-Ho Cho
pmc-13605439.description: Background/Objectives: Prototype-based few-shot segmentation is validated almost entirely on centimetre-scale abdominal organs; on pulmonary nodules, 70% of which are less than 10 mm in size, accuracy degrades sharply. We seek to determine how much of that degradation is geometric rather than methodological. Methods: No published method is trained or evaluated here.
